Women do have significant gender related issues, however the media does like to blow things out of proportion. It's not terrible but it's not great. For example The abortion clinics in Texas is a pretty big issue, considering you know 2nd most populated state with the 2nd most area... if someone lived in midwest texas they essentially have to make a day trip to have an abortion.

It would be great if women didn't have to spend a day to get an abortion, but they have a time period of 14-24 weeks to do it, so it's not very time sensitive. Having a clinic closer to you seems like a luxury, at least when you compare it to how it was in the past, and how it is in other countries.

I looked at a map of abortion clinics in Texas, and they all seem to be on the edge of the state. Why aren't there any abortion clinics closer to the center?
It's not a luxury when the state of texas is making near impossible standards to open up new centers, they essentially need to be hospital/surgical centers to exist in the state...

If there are unreasonable standards that prevents someone from opening a clinic, then that's a different a problem. Do those standards only apply to abortion clinics? Are there similar standards for other businesses?

Are those standards there to make is safer to have an abortion, or to limit the amount of clinics in the state?

Consider some women have to drive hundreds of miles and not everyone has the financial capabilities of doing so. They also may be required to wait for a day (so get a hotel room) and have a sonogram of their fetus, even if it is in the very early stages. There was also controversy about a mandatory vaginal probe. The regulations are a sneaky way of forbidding abortion because politicians can't outright ban it. Liken this to a hypothetical: in a more progressive state, regulations make purchasing a gun extremely inconvenient. It's a sneaky way to enforce law that can't legitimately be made.

My personal feelings are that "cheap" is not a valid point, when you talk about a right to "cheap" things, I almost always disagree with someone. For instance there is a right for you to get a sex change, that doesn't mean the government should have to subsidize it. When the government subsidizes medicine it is circumventing the market, if you want more affordable BC then the gov should get out of the market then the B.C. manufacturers will drop their prices to compete with the emerging manufacturers.

Availability is more important, like the lack of availability of men's shelters. I think feminism has lost its purpose, first it was for suffrage, then for equal workplace rights, but now if you ask feminists what they want the answer is always different and if you ask for what laws they'd like implemented (in my experience) they don't have a specific example or the ones they provide are ludicrous (such as banning urinals or mandatory do not rape classes)

AstroVortex, I'm glad to see you.

Undoubtedly, women have it worse in places like Saudi Arabia, where they cannot drive without a man's written permission, than in first world countries. But I believe feminism is still needed. No part of feminism says that all men have it better than all women, or that men don't have problems. It is a movement for equality that has been ongoing for decades. Equality means equality for both sexes. Feminists care about men's issues because they are oftentimes the result of the same mechanisms that cause issues for women. Gender roles, for instance, tell boys they have to be tough. Girls are associated with weakness. Not by accident, one of the worst things you can be called is a pussy -- a girl's anatomy (which is about as changeable as skin color). Consider some of the problems MRAs talk about: Men are much more likely to be sentenced to death in the US, male rape isn't taken seriously; both of these can be at least partially attributed to the application of gender roles. We assume men are tough and are more violent and more able to stand up for themselves and there's no way they could be overpowered. You see how damaging the gender roles can be? Think about how culturally, women are subjugated everywhere. They are thought of as worse drivers (even though men have to pay higher insurance because they have more wrecks because they drive more aggressively maybe because of gender stereotypes), "crazy"/overemotional, you can fill in the blanks. Women have to worry about their looks so much more and in many ways. What does what I'm wearing say about my sexual availability? Will people call me a slut for wearing this or say I'm asking to be raped?

Beyond the personal things women have to go through every day, think about women in a larger social context. 80% of the Senate is male, but 50% of the population is male. Female lawyers are paid less than their male counterparts in similar positions, and that gap increases along with the prestige of their position. Female CEOs are also much less common, as are billionaires. All of these things get worse if you look at women of color. (the .1% black female billionaires in the US is Oprah).

I was a little all over the board with this answer, and partly that's because feminist studies is a huge area that covers many topics. It doesn't make sense to be ignorant of all of it. You don't have to agree with everything you read, but there are a thousand things worth considering you've never even though of. Privilege is not having to think about these things because they don't happen to you. If you're truly interested in learning something about feminism, take an intro to feminist studies class, or read a book. Borderlands by Gloria Anzaldua is one; if you're more attune to watching a video here is an interesting talk. Ignorance is easy. Happy Hunting!

I have a very open mind. I want everyone to be equal.

It's not men's fault there are less women in those professions, it's most likely because women don't want those professions. Now, the reason they don't want those professions is because of standards set by other women.

And when it comes to billionaires, a fortune like takes takes many generations, or an invention/idea. There is no one stopping women from inventing things, or having ideas.
